name: csv-write
algorithm: Generate R records of 8 fields once (splitmix64 from seed 42; each field 0 to 11 bytes over letters, digits, space, comma, quote and LF, so about a third need quotes), then write them reps times as CSV through each standard library's writer into an in-memory buffer cleared per rep (Mk csv.WriteRecord into a Text through its Writer; Go encoding/csv Writer into a bytes.Buffer); then read the last output back through a file with the same library's reader and print the records, the fields, the field bytes and the sum of the field bytes.

skip.mk-wrap: the generator already uses the wrapping operators; the counts stay below 2^34
skip.c: no std CSV writer in C; no hand-written writer stands in (tests/bench/README.md 'No stand-ins')
skip.rust: Rust std has no CSV writer; the csv crate is not std (no stand-ins)
skip.zig: no std CSV writer in Zig

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries; the checksum is over the values read back (B18), since the writers quote differently (Go also quotes a field that starts with a space, and writes LF line ends where Mk writes CR LF)
notes: Added for review finding csv-5: WriteRecord had no row. The emitted WriteCsv of gen csv.Codec writes each field as WriteRecord does (codec.mk's field writer), so this row measures its field path too.

The generation and the read-back run once, inside the program's time; the reps measure the writer. An informal split on the owner's machine (2026-11-12, busy, min of 5 runs each, 200000 records, reps 1 against 21): Mk 58.8 ms a rep, Go 53.2 ms a rep. Not published: no number here is a measurement until tools/bench publish runs.
Written by std-csv, M8, 2026-11-12; checksums from both columns' runs, which agree.
